module.purpose: Provides a UI component in the event-types feature that lets users add a verified email address. It collects an email, validates its format, triggers a verification code flow, and on successful code verification persists the email as verified for the event type context.
module.summary: AddVerifiedEmail is a React function component used within the event types feature of Cal.com. It renders a labeled TextField where a user types an email address, with an arrow-right Button (wrapped in a Tooltip) that, when clicked, validates the email against a simple regex and opens a verification modal. The component composes several platform atom hooks: useGetVerifiedEmails to refetch the verified email list, useAddVerifiedEmail to persist a newly verified email (showing success or error toasts), useVerifyEmail to send the verification email (optionally addressed to the provided username), and useVerifyCode to handle code submission. On successful code verification it closes the modal, clears the input, and calls addVerifiedEmail. The VerifyCodeDialog component manages the code-entry UI, configured so user session is not required to verify. The component relies on useLocale for translations and showToast for feedback.
module.businessContext: Part of the Cal.com scheduling product: event types can require attendees/bookers to use verified email addresses. This component ensures emails added to an event type are verified via a code, preventing spoofed or unowned addresses. If it fails, users cannot attach verified emails to event types.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Clicking the add-verified-emails button with a valid, non-empty email opens the verification dialog and starts email verification.
moduleContractTests.when: click the addOnSuffix button in the add-verified-emails text field
moduleContractTests.then: isEmailVerificationModalVisible becomes true and handleVerifyEmail() is invoked
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins the trigger path from UI input to verification flow.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An email failing the /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ pattern must not open the dialog or trigger verification.
moduleContractTests.then: isEmailVerificationModalVisible stays false and handleVerifyEmail() is not called
moduleContractTests.rationale: Guards against starting verification with malformed input.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An empty email input must not open the verification dialog.
moduleContractTests.then: isEmailVerificationModalVisible stays false and handleVerifyEmail() is not called
moduleContractTests.rationale: Empty-input edge case of the !!verifiedEmail guard.

moduleContractTests.scenario: When code verification succeeds, the dialog closes, the input is cleared, the email is added, and verified-emails are refetched.
moduleContractTests.then: dialog closes, verifiedEmail resets to "", addVerifiedEmail({ email: verifiedEmail }) is awaited, refetchVerifiedEmails() is called, and showToast(t("email_verified"), "success") fires
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins the full success flow including toast and refetch ordering.
